content.text: This confirms tainted `param` from request flows directly into XPath query string without sanitization, used in `root.xpath(query)`.

input.justification: The value `param` is taken directly from `request.form.getlist("BenchmarkTest00207")` (user-controlled input) and assigned to `bar` in multiple branches of the match statement without any sanitization or escaping. `bar` is then interpolated directly into an XPath expression string via an f-string (`f'/Employees/Employee[@emplid=\'{bar}\']'`), which is passed to `root.xpath(query)`. There is no validation, escaping, or parameterization of the value before it reaches the XPath sink, so a malicious user could inject XPath syntax (e.g., `' or '1'='1`) to alter query logic or exfiltrate data. This matches the classic XPath injection pattern and the taint flow is direct and unbroken.
